source.title: To understand deep learning we need to understand kernel learning
source.authors: Mikhail Belkin; Si-Yuan Ma; Soumik Mandal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label fitting and training time in kernel methods, a different model family used to examine parallels with deep networks. The paper's own experiments do not test deep networks.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior ReLU-network random-label results but does not reproduce them. Its own random-label experiments use Laplacian and Gaussian kernels; these are recorded under fits_no_version because the claim versions specify deep networks.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments and theoretical results concern kernel classifiers, not standard deep networks. It discusses parallels with the claim and cites the original neural-network findings, but does not test any supplied version in the specified system class.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that Laplacian kernels fit random labels relatively quickly, whereas Gaussian kernels require substantially more epochs. Similar test performance despite these optimization differences motivates their argument that kernel structure and inductive bias deserve attention in explaining generalization, and that understanding kernels may inform understanding deep networks. Their own experiments do not test deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: Kernel classifiers trained with EigenPro-SGD or direct interpolation; the paper compares kernel results with cited prior neural-network results rather than running the original deep-network method.
record.method_sensitivity: Kernel smoothness changes the optimization cost: Gaussian kernels take many more epochs than Laplacian kernels to fit random labels. Dataset also changes the reported epoch counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Laplacian kernels reach zero training classification error in 7, 21, and 4 epochs with random labels, versus 4, 8, and 3 with original labels on MNIST, SVHN, and TIMIT. Gaussian kernels require 873, 1066, and 22 epochs, versus 20, 46, and 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel classifiers fit random labels, with substantially different optimization costs depending on kernel smoothness and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 4.1 and 5 report strong generalization of overfitted and interpolated kernel classifiers under added label noise, with similar Gaussian and Laplacian test performance despite different optimization costs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel classifiers can retain useful generalization while fitting noisy training labels exactly; optimization speed alone does not explain their test performance.

record.problems: The random-label results are for kernel methods, not deep networks. The paper reports epoch counts but no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows needed; the tables report one original-label and one random-label epoch count for each kernel-dataset pair, all extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters in standard deep networks.
Deep-network training-time ratios and convergence as label corruption increases.
Deep-network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across label-noise levels in deep networks.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization in deep networks.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels in deep networks.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Kernel interpretations as fixed-first-layer two-layer networks do not meet the supplied standard-deep-network scope. The states describe inability to adjudicate these versions, not failure of the kernels to fit random labels. Excerpt E1 exceeds the quote limit and repeats a prose claim contradicted by the SVHN table entry.

versions.untested_parts: Deep networks; the paper's random-label experiments are on kernel methods.
Deep networks; the paper's epoch comparisons are on kernel methods.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
No sweep from clean to fully randomized labels testing the stated training-fit and test-error pattern in deep networks.
No test of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on deep networks fitting random labels.
No experiment testing the order in which deep networks learn real patterns and label noise.
